title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 1986 'Analysis situs (troisième mouture)' Grothendieck axiomatizes a 'magasin' (store). This is a set M of 'pieces' (tame/polyhedral regions) with three relations: X ≤ Y (part of), X ≪ Y (relatively compact or 'well inside' inclusion) and a third relation. That third relation can be either ≬ ('apart' or separated, i.e. disjoint closures) or |o| (non-overlapping, i.e. disjoint interiors). Further notation:
- L is a set of elementary pieces or cells (atoms).
- comb(X) is the set of cells making up X, and comb(X)° its interior cells.
- X̃ is the combinatorial decomposition of X.
- x ∥ y is a basic separation relation on cells.
Axioms L1–L3 give the cellular or atomic structure. Page 105 showed that, under L1–L3, one can define X |o| Y by: for all x in comb(X)° and y in comb(Y)°, x ∥ y. It also showed that the original ≬ coincides with the ≬' recovered from |o| by a second formula. That formula takes L = X̃ ∧ Ỹ and uses the decomposition comb(X) \ comb(L) = ∪_{X' ∈ X̃\L} comb(X')°.

This page is a 'Scholie' summarizing the comparison of the two axiomatic viewpoints.
(*) From a ≬-magasin satisfying L1–L3 one gets a |o|-magasin: X |o| Y iff all interior cells of X and of Y are pairwise ∥.
(**) Conversely, a |o|-magasin, under an extra condition, gives a ≬-magasin. In the main text the definition reads: X ∥ Y iff X' |o| Y' for all X' ∈ X̃, Y' ∈ Ỹ. The marginal corrected version reads: X ≬ Y iff X'' |o| Y'' for all X'' ∈ X̃ \ (X̃∧Ỹ) and Y'' ∈ Ỹ \ (X̃∧Ỹ). In words, two pieces are apart iff the parts of their decompositions outside the common refinement have disjoint interiors.

The round trip is not the identity in general. A general |o| cannot be reconstructed from the ≤, ≪, ≬ it induces. For that one needs Mag 6'', a 'divisibility' or atomic-determination condition, written (****): X |o| Y iff x |o| y for all x ∈ comb(X)°, y ∈ comb(Y)°. In other words, |o| is induced by its restriction to cells, where it equals ∥. He notes that Mag 6'' implies AtL1, and that it holds only if 'addition' (union of pieces) satisfies divisibility.

The next page concludes with an equivalence of categories:
- ≬-magasins satisfying AtL1, L2, L3 and AtC(spec), and
- |o|-magasins satisfying (****).
Grothendieck judges this common structure 'too restrictive' because of AtL1 (atomicity).

Purpose: choosing which primitive relation should found a combinatorial-topological ('tame') analysis situs, by comparing the separation-based and the overlap-based axiomatics.
errors: The main-text (**) writes X ∥ Y over all X' ∈ X̃, Y' ∈ Ỹ. The marginal correction, consistent with p.105, restricts to pieces outside X̃∧Ỹ and defines ≬, not ∥. As first written, the formula would make any two pieces sharing a cell non-separated in a way that conflicts with p.105.
The 'condition supplémentaire' needed for the |o| → ≬ direction is not specified on this page. It appears to be the same divisibility/atomicity condition, but this is left implicit.
Claims such as 'Mag 6'' implies AtL1' are asserted without proof here (partly argued on p.107). The argument there that comb(X)° ≠ ∅ uses Mag 5'' (irreflexivity of |o|) and is only sketched.

ideas.what: Two alternative axiomatizations of a region-based 'store' of pieces. Both use part-of (≤) and well-inside (≪); the third primitive is either apartness (≬) or non-overlap of interiors (|o|).
ideas.modern_name: Mereotopology / region connection calculus (part P, non-tangential proper part NTPP, disconnected DC vs discrete DR); contact algebras and proximity (strong inclusion ≪)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (1929), de Laguna, Clarke (1981), Randell–Cui–Cohn RCC (1992); de Vries (1962) compingent algebras; Efremovič proximity; Dimov–Vakarelov contact algebras (2006)
ideas.where_published: Only in the Montpellier analysis situs manuscripts. Esquisse d'un programme calls for 'topologie modérée' but contains no such axiomatics.

ideas.what: Comparison functors between the two kinds of structures, with an equivalence of categories on the subclasses satisfying atomic-determination (divisibility) axioms.
ideas.modern_name: Duality/equivalence between contact (DC-based) and overlap (DR-based) mereotopologies; atomic mereotopologies determined by adjacency of atoms (cell complexes / adjacency graphs)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Düntsch, Winter, Vakarelov, Stell, Galton (2000s) for contact vs. overlap relations and atomic or discrete mereotopology

ideas.what: Condition (****) / Mag 6'': the non-overlap relation between pieces is determined by its restriction to interior cells, i.e. induced by a relation ∥ on the set L of atoms.
ideas.modern_name: Atomicity / locality of the contact relation: the relation is generated by an adjacency relation on cells (as in digital and discrete topology, abstract cell complexes)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'magasins (≤, ≪, ≬ / |o|)' form an independent axiomatization of what is now called mereotopology or contact algebra. The relations are part-of, well-inside (non-tangential part) and disconnection vs. disjoint interiors. The page compares the DC-based and DR-based primitives and finds an equivalence only under atomicity. The literature on tame topology and Grothendieck's analysis situs does not appear to have linked these notes to the mereotopology / region-connection-calculus / de Vries-duality tradition.
missed.quote: Scholie sur la comparaison des points de vue de "Magasins ≤, ≪, ≬" et "Magasins ≤, ≪, |o|"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: His 1986 work could be read alongside contact algebras and point-free topology (de Vries duality, Dimov–Vakarelov). His dissatisfaction with atomicity (AtL1) anticipates the move to atomless contact algebras as models of regular-closed regions.

missed.claim: Grothendieck finds the common domain of the two notions 'too restrictive' because it forces AtL1 (atomicity). The search for a non-atomic framework in which apartness and non-overlap are interdefinable is left open.
missed.quote: Ceci n'est possible que si l'addition satisfait la condition de divisibilité
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: In atomless contact algebras the relation between C (contact) and overlap is a known subtle point. A precise statement of when ≬ and |o| determine each other, without atoms, is a natural question.

deep.surprise_reason: The scholium is a careful comparison of two primitive-relation axiomatics for a combinatorial analysis situs, ending in an equivalence of categories under atomicity. Its main interest is the unnoticed parallel with mereotopology and contact algebras. The mathematics itself is fairly routine order-theoretic bookkeeping.

Marginal formula should read: '(**) X ≬ Y ⟺ ∀ X'' ∈ X̃ \ X̃∧Ỹ, Y'' ∈ Ỹ \ X̃∧Ỹ, on a X'|o|Y'' (set difference with X̃∧Ỹ, not '∩ X̃∘Ỹ').
